clue.text: Sailor's poem, ie merchantman therefore in it at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaman's verse describes a merchant vessel sailing on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the twenty-six letters of IE MERCHANTMAN THEREFORE IN IT; the nautical words make the fodder look like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's 1798 ballad is narrated by an old seaman who shot an albatross, so it is literally a seafarer's poem.

clue.text: Support topless parts of female cyberpunks

indicators.note: parts is read as a verb, splitting the female's word in two so another piece sits between

parts.note: something of a female is hers

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, so the first letter of the support word is dropped

parts.note: to back is to support

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to promise some racy cyberpunk underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides that 'parts' is a verb: the trimmed support word splits the female's word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberpunks are computer-savvy rebels, the sort of people who break into systems illicitly.

clue.text: Regularly ordered doctor on ship to return to it

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following word, here the even ones

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: A doctor is ordered back aboard the vessel he has just left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of 'ordered'; 'on' places the doctor above the ship in this down clue, and 'it' in the definition points back to that ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a vessel again after leaving it is to go back onto the ship.

clue.text: Baby's ability to talk?

indicators.note: to talk means the word is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds the same as the synonym

parts.note: might is power or ability

explanation.surface: A question about whether an infant can speak yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; the surface reads it as a possessive about the baby's talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is an affectionate word for a very small child.

clue.text: Under big dam, reset faulty pressure gauges?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under others is written after them

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for big sizes
a dam is an animal's mother, and mom is the American word for mother

indicators.note: faulty signals that the letters of the following word are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: Faulty gauges below a large dam need to be reset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places the anagram of RESET (ETERS) below OS + MOM; the question mark flags that these gauges measure osmotic pressure specifically.
explanation.definitionFit: An osmometer measures osmotic pressure, so these instruments are a specialised kind of pressure meter.

clue.text: Light meat or cheese sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches is a verb here: the words meat or cheese hold the letters between them

explanation.surface: A recommendation for a light lunch of meat or cheese sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but means 'holds inside': the answer is buried across meaT OR CHeese. 'Light' is a noun, not an adjective about the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp, a hand-held source of light.

clue.text: Sanction refusal to replace first-class honour

indicators.note: to replace tells us one piece takes the place of another inside the main word

parts.note: to enable is to sanction or allow
A is first-class, as in A1 or A-grade
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to approve the replacement of a top honour.
explanation.walkthrough: NO (refusal) takes the place of the A (first-class) in ENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage is a great distinction, so the verb means to honour or dignify.

clue.text: Running around North Dakota, one goes out with it

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for around
ND is the US postal abbreviation for North Dakota
I is the Roman numeral for one
to go out with someone is to date them
with it means fashionable, which is hip

explanation.surface: A jogger circles North Dakota alongside a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' is the definition, in the sense of standing for election, not jogging; 'around' gives CA rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Running for office means standing as a contender, the state of being a nominee.

clue.text: Young European about study Cologne

indicators.note: about means the European goes round the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
to read a subject is to study it at university
cologne is a perfume, a scent

explanation.surface: A young European is studying in the German city of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne looks like the German city, but it is eau de Cologne, a perfume; 'about' has the European wrapped round the study word.
explanation.definitionFit: A child just before puberty is still young, not yet a teenager.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
Date little British misfit

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A diminutive British oddball goes on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a socially awkward, unfashionable person who does not fit in.

clue.text: Cold-blooded types speed into main road, almost diagonal

indicators.note: into means the speed piece goes inside the main road piece

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, with the 1 read as the letter I
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for diagonal is dropped

parts.note: a bias is a diagonal line across the weave of fabric

explanation.surface: Reptiles race onto a highway, crossing it at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's Great North Road, the longest numbered road in the country; 'into' and 'almost' each signal their own step.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs, toads and newts are cold-blooded animals, and this is the zoological class containing them.

clue.text: Builder to drool over ass? Spooner would say so

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words are switched at their starts

parts.note: to drool over something is to want to lick it
an ass brays, so it is a brayer

explanation.surface: A builder slobbers over a donkey, or so Spooner would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the openings of LICK BRAYER: L and BR change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer is a tradesman who builds walls from bricks and mortar.

clue.text: In retreat, began to bury reserve soldiers

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the whole assembled word is read from the end
to bury means the reserve piece goes inside the word for began

parts.note: began means started

explanation.surface: Troops in retreat set about burying their reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bury' puts RES into STARTED (STARTRESED), and 'In retreat' reverses the lot. The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were a famous British armoured division of the Second World War, a body of troops.

clue.text: Imitating the French Resistance, start to occupy squat

parts.note: ze is how 'the' sounds in a mock French accent
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: start to means taking the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters copy the French tactic of squatting in occupied buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French Resistance' looks like one phrase but splits: ZE imitates a French speaker saying 'the'. 'squat' is the British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat is slang for nothing, as in 'he knows squat', which is nil.

clue.text: Eggheads enlightened — are upset with this, oddly

parts.note: lit means lighted up, enlightened

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word are is read from the bottom
oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Intellectuals are oddly troubled by this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ARE into ERA, and 'oddly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of 'this', T and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read intellectuals, people of letters, the cultured elite.

clue.text: Gather food

definitions.meaning: to gather fabric into a fold
British slang for snacks, especially at school

explanation.definitionFit: Sewing sense: a tuck is a stitched fold, made by gathering cloth; schoolboy slang: tuck means sweets and snacks.

clue.text: Primarily "cat" suggests "kitty"

definitions.note: kitty is a single fund while the answer is a plural noun for funds, which still serves as a collective

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to offer is to suggest or propose

explanation.surface: Calling a cat a kitty, as a first suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitty' is not a young cat but a pool of money, the definition; the quotation marks make it look like a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared pot of money, and coffers are a store of funds or treasury.

clue.text: A decanter I smashed, being unhinged

indicators.note: smashed means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who smashes a wine decanter must be out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhinged' looks like 'mad', but it is literal: a bivalve shell with no hinge teeth. 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In zoology an ecardinate shell lacks the teeth that form a hinge, so it is literally without a hinge.

clue.text: An image that embodies "sexy" without light

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving the letter A

indicators.note: that embodies means the image word contains the other piece in its body

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image
hot means sexy

explanation.surface: A picture capturing sex appeal, taken in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that embodies' makes the image word a container; 'An' supplies the opening letter on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphotic describes deep ocean zones where sunlight never reaches, so they are utterly dark.

clue.text: Cry that foot's broken before every game

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the next one
broken means the cry word is split open with the other piece inside

parts.note: to sob is to cry
FT is the abbreviation for foot
all means every

explanation.surface: Someone yelps that their foot is broken before every match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like an injury but signals that the cry word is split open, with the foot abbreviation set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Softball is a variant of baseball played with a larger ball, a team sport.

clue.text: Stick (at the crease?)

definitions.meaning: a rod, as passed in a relay or waved by a conductor
the crease is the line where a cricket batsman stands, so staying there is to carry on batting

explanation.definitionFit: A rod is passed between relay runners; split in two, the letters say to keep batting in cricket, still in at the crease.

clue.text: Moral fibre ultimately stupid? Almost

definitions.note: moral is a noun here, a principle of right conduct

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so only the last letter of the following word is taken
almost means the final letter of the stupid word is dropped

parts.note: thick means stupid

explanation.surface: A question whether lacking moral fibre is nearly stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moral fibre' looks like a single phrase, but 'Moral' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral is a principle of conduct, and an ethic is a set of principles guiding behaviour.

clue.text: Avoid accident when junction's blocked?

indicators.note: blocked means the junction is cut off, taking its letter away from the word

parts.note: a shunt is British slang for a minor car crash
T stands for a T-junction

explanation.surface: Drivers avoid a crash where a road junction is blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: A shunt is everyday British slang for a minor car crash; taking away T (a T-junction) leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun something is to keep away from it deliberately, steering clear of it.

clue.text: A number of French & Italian men cry as it's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: French and Italian men weep as a song is played on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is a song; the anagram uses OF FRENCH and ITALIAN MEN CRY AS IT'S, with the & left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song in a performer's repertoire; this is Tony Bennett's famous ballad about a Californian city.
